quote: each Party shall have the right to exploit, including license, the Joint Program Technology, without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent from the other Party to exploit such Joint Program Technology. quote: either Party may request in writing and the non-requesting Party shall (at the non-requesting Party's election), with respect to Confidential Information to which such non-requesting Party does not retain rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement (if applicable, with respect to the terminated Region or terminated Product) promptly destroy all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession or control of the non-requesting Party and confirm such destruction in writing to the requesting Party.
rationale: The Agreement contains a comprehensive exit regime, so nothing is missing. Section 11.6 (which expressly survives under Section 12.4) is reciprocal: on termination either Party — including us — may require the other to destroy all copies of our Confidential Information (data, know-how, reports) that it has no surviving right to retain and to certify that destruction in writing, with retention limited to archival/back-up copies and continuing obligations. That satisfies the data-return/deletion-certification limb at or above the fallback; deletion is only on our request, so there is no walk-away risk of unilateral or immediate deletion of our data. On the assistance limb, the direction of travel reflects the reversion bargain rather than a gap: because we are RevMed's licensee, on termination the Products revert to RevMed, so Sections 12.3(c)(iv)–(vi) put the transition-assistance, regulatory-transfer, data-transfer, manufacturing and sell-off obligations on us (we should not seek to flag or expand obligations that bind us), while Section 12.3(b) makes our licenses perpetual and royalty-free on expiry, Section 12.3(c)(iii)/(d)(ii) give us a post-termination sell-off period, and Section 12.3(e) requires RevMed to give us copies of the relevant data and "all reasonable assistance" in the change-of-control scenario where we do retain the program. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than redlined: Section 11.6 provides for destruction only (no return/export of copies in a machine-readable format) and uses "promptly" rather than a fixed 30-day outside date, and Section 12.3(d)(i) gives us a license on termination for RevMed's breach or insolvency without an accompanying know-how/data delivery (partly mitigated by the Section 7.2 manufacturing know-how transfer). Neither is material enough to fail the fallback.

quote: 13.5 No Other Warranties. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII, (A) NO REPRESENTATION, CONDITION OR WARRANTY WHATSOEVER IS MADE OR GIVEN BY OR ON BEHALF OF SANOFI OR REVMED; AND (B) ALL OTHER CONDITIONS AND WARRANTIES WHETHER WRITTEN OR ORAL OR EXPRESS OR IMPLIED ARE HEREBY EXPRESSLY EXCLUDED, INCLUDING ANY CONDITIONS AND WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT.
rationale: The rule is met at or above the preferred position, as translated to this collaboration/license structure. RevMed gives an extensive, one-way express warranty package in §13.2 (sole and exclusive ownership of RevMed Background Technology free of liens, no prior encumbrance or conflicting grant, right to grant the licenses, non-infringement and non-misappropriation to its Knowledge, patent validity and proper prosecution/maintenance, no litigation or adverse proceedings, no government funding/Bayh-Dole taint, data-room completeness, and §13.2(u) material compliance with all Applicable Law in the conduct of all R&D), reinforced by the §13.1(c)-(e) FCPA/Excluded List/permits reps and the §13.4 mutual no-debarment and Applicable Law compliance covenants. The "professional and workmanlike" analogue is present as a substantive performance standard: p0291 and p0313 require all Research and Development activities to be performed in compliance with Applicable Law including GMP, GLP and GCP, with diligent efforts against the applicable Plan timelines. A real remedy exists: §14.1(b)-(c) gives us indemnification for material breach of RevMed's warranties or obligations, and §12.6 confirms termination is not the sole remedy and that all other remedies remain available, so ordinary damages and specific performance survive. Critically, the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty: §13.5 is mutual (it protects Sanofi equally) and is expressly prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII," so the Article XIII warranties are fully carved out — this is nowhere near the "AS IS" walk-away. Noted for the file rather than flagged: there is no fixed conformance-to-documentation warranty period, no repair/replace/refund mechanic and no malicious-code warranty, but those preferred sub-elements are artifacts of a software/services deal and have no application to a research collaboration with no software or fixed deliverables; product quality and GMP conformance warranties are deliberately and appropriately deferred to the Supply Agreement and Quality Agreement to be negotiated under §7.3, which is the customary and correct home for them. No redline warranted.

quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated at all times during which any SHP2 Inhibitors or Product is being clinically tested in human subjects or commercially distributed or sold. Sanofi may fulfill such obligation through self- insurance. Each Party shall provide the other Party with evidence of such insurance upon request
rationale: A usable insurance covenant exists at Section 14.6, so the rule is not missing. RevMed must procure and maintain insurance (expressly including product liability cover) appropriate to its activities under the Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements, for the whole period during which any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product is in human clinical testing or is commercially distributed or sold — i.e. coverage matched to the actual risk profile of this collaboration rather than the CGL/E&O/cyber stack contemplated by the preferred position, which is calibrated to services/hosting vendors processing Customer Data. RevMed is not a data processor or on-premises services vendor here, so walk-away territory is not engaged. The clause also delivers the key customer-side protections: evidence of insurance on request (equivalent to certificates on request), advance written notice from RevMed of cancellation, non-renewal or material change, and an express statement that the insurance does not cap RevMed's indemnification obligations under Article XIV. Two features are affirmatively in our favour and are not flagged: the self-insurance option is available to Sanofi only, and the cancellation-notice obligation runs one way against RevMed. Noted but not flagged as deviations: the clause states no dollar limits (relying on the "normal business practices of companies similarly situated" standard, which is market for this deal type) and has no express one-year tail beyond the coverage period, which is partly mitigated because the obligation runs for as long as Product is tested or sold. On its material terms the clause meets the rule's intent at the fallback level, so we are not redlining it.
